name: core
notes: options.active_plugins/template/stylesheet (task #39, docs/proposals/code-half.md §3.1): the cross-partition invariant DESIGN.md §3.4 names (active_plugins ⊆ plugins in code/) needs these captured, but applying them via direct SQL is actively wrong — activate_plugin()/switch_theme() do real one-time setup in register_activation_hook/switch_theme/after_switch_theme that a raw UPDATE wp_options would skip while leaving WordPress believing the plugin/theme is active. Classified managed (the same class _menu_item_* and _wp_attached_file already use for 'authored-domain fact, bespoke capture/apply handling'): Capture::build_options() reads them with bespoke code alongside (not through) the authored-options whitelist loop; Apply::apply_options() excludes them from the generic direct-SQL upsert loop; only agent/src/Deploy.php's `wp duo deploy` reconciles them, via real WP APIs, deliberately outside Canary::arm()/disarm() — activation hooks must fire there, and apply's canary requires the opposite. Values are plain portable strings (plugin file paths, theme directory slugs) — no ref-tokenization, since that stability across environments IS the invariant.

post_meta.wp_pattern_sync_status (task #31): Site-Editor-only flag on wp_block posts, verified empirically on a running install (e1, WP core 7.0.2, wp-includes/post.php's wp_create_initial_post_meta() — no plugin involved, registered unconditionally regardless of active theme). register_post_meta('wp_block', 'wp_pattern_sync_status', ['type'=>'string','single'=>true,'sanitize_callback'=>'sanitize_text_field','show_in_rest'=>['schema'=>['type'=>'string','enum'=>['partial','unsynced']]]]). Confirmed by direct DB read: a fresh wp_block post carries ZERO postmeta rows at all — the default 'fully synced' pattern state is the KEY'S ABSENCE, not a value like 'full'/'synced' (there is no such value in the enum). Once set, the value is a plain, non-serialized scalar string ('unsynced' or 'partial') sitting directly in wp_postmeta.meta_value — confirmed both via direct meta (`wp post meta update`) and via the REST route (WP_REST_Blocks_Controller::filter_response_by_context() promotes meta.wp_pattern_sync_status to a top-level response property and strips it from the meta sub-object on READ, but WRITES still go through the ordinary meta sub-object — verified empirically with an authenticated rest_do_request() POST carrying {"meta":{"wp_pattern_sync_status":"partial"}}, which persisted to the same postmeta row read back via get_post_meta()). Classified authored, plain (no ref — it's a flag, not an id) — the existing generic no-ref post_meta path (tokenize_text() on a scalar string, a no-op here since 'unsynced'/'partial' contain no env-bound substring) already round-trips it correctly with zero new engine code, exactly like _wp_page_template.

shortcode_attrs.gallery (DUO-3259): the LEGACY [gallery ...] SHORTCODE's four genuine reference-shaped attributes, grounded via direct read of WordPress 7.0.2's real wp-includes/media.php gallery_shortcode() source, not assumed — distinct from (and complementary to, not redundant with) block_attrs['core/gallery']'s own 'ids' entry above, which covers the separate GUTENBERG BLOCK's own JSON-attribute schema; one is raw shortcode text sitting in post_content, the other a parsed block attribute, two different WordPress mechanisms that happen to share a display name. 'id' defaults to the CURRENT post when the attribute is absent (used as post_parent for get_children() once include/exclude are unset) — an implicit self-reference needing no rewrite at all, since it resolves correctly against the same post's own regenerated id after apply for free; an omitted 'id' is therefore never flagged by lint or the unscoped-ref gate, only a LITERAL numeric 'id="N"' is rewritten. 'ids' is aliased verbatim into 'include' when non-empty (`$attr['include'] = $attr['ids'];`, read directly in gallery_shortcode()) — both share the exact same comma-separated-post-id format 'include' and 'exclude' also use, fed straight to get_posts()/get_children(). img_caption_shortcode()'s own 'id' attribute (the [caption id="..."] shape DUO-3259 was originally filed assuming needed an equivalent codec) is DELIBERATELY NOT declared here: confirmed by reading img_caption_shortcode() directly, that attribute is sanitize_html_class()'d and emitted verbatim as a DOM id for CSS/JS targeting only — never parsed back into a numeric attachment reference anywhere in WordPress core. There is nothing to codec; 'caption' is ruled explicitly unsupported for that reason (no reference-shaped attribute exists to declare), not because a codec for it would be hard to build.

menu_fields.locations (DUO-3272): the v0 baseline for every menu's location assignment — captured from the active theme's raw theme_mods_<stylesheet>['nav_menu_locations'] (Capture::scope_menus()), applied via a direct Db::update/insert write (Apply::assign_locations(), deliberately hook-free like every other product-database mutation). This is the ordinary, correct behavior for every site with no plugin managing per-language menu state. A pinned plugin manifest may reclassify this field 'derived' when it can prove the raw slot is actually a mutable projection THAT plugin's own machinery rewrites at will (Polylang: see manifests/polylang.json's own note, and Policy::menu_field_class()'s docblock, and the DUO-3272 issue for the full empirical grounding) — Policy::active_menu_field_reclassifications() surfaces any such override as a loud plan warning, the same DUO-3249 precedence and transparency mechanism options.default_category already uses.
